description:
FILED s463au (agent AU, round 20), found by the #962 acceptance battery.
PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to #962 (probed on the 6e6f191 base tree, where the
whole family was wrong; after #962 only the printf spelling is).

    $_ = 'aaaccc';
    printf("%s|%s\n", /zzz/, "b", "c");   perl: b|c      PCL: |b
    print sprintf("%s|%s\n", /zzz/, "b", "c");  BOTH b|c
    print "C:", join("|", /zzz/, "b"), "\n";    BOTH b
    print "A:", /zzz/, "|", /a/, "\n";          BOTH |1
    warn "E:", /zzz/, "b", "\n";                BOTH b

MECHANISM: `p-printf`'s ARGUMENTS ARE NOT EVALUATED IN LIST CONTEXT.  Compare
the emissions of the two print-family spellings for the same operand:

    (p-print "A:" (p-list-ctx (p-=~ $_ (p-regex "/zzz/"))) "|" â¦)
    (p-printf "B:%s|%s\n" (p-=~ $_ (p-regex "/zzz/")) "b" "c")

so the match runs in whatever context is ambient (scalar/void at a statement
root) and answers the scalar `""` â one phantom argument, and every later
argument shifts by one.  perl evaluates a list operator's arguments in LIST
context, and PCL's own `print` arm proves the machinery exists; `printf` and
`warn` (same emission shape, checked) do not get it.  The context is set from
`get_node_context($node_id)` in `Pl::ExprToCL` (ctx_bind), so the miss is in
what marks printf's argument nodes LIST_CTX â PExpr's context propagation, not
the runtime.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND printf: any context-SENSITIVE operand in a printf
argument list is affected â a failed m// (above), `readline` (scalar reads one
record where perl reads all), a sub whose body asks `wantarray`, `caller`,
`each`, `p-backtick`/`qx`.  A raw @array argument is NOT affected
(p-flatten-args spreads it whatever the context), which is why the bug is
invisible in the common case and why nothing in the sweep moves on it.

CLAUDE.md 11 is the shape of the fix: `print`/`say`/`printf` are named in the
rule itself as "the list-operator filehandle family", so this is one family
with one member missing, not a printf special case.  `warn`/`die` are the same
question one step out.

BAR: the five rows above; `printf "%s", <FH>` and a `wantarray`-visible sub in
a printf argument list; `printf "%s|%s", @a` unchanged (the raw-array spelling
that works today); corpus-diff + emission A/B over the four populations, since
this ADDS a context bind to every printf call site.

MEASURED with a wantarray-visible sub, which discriminates where the failed
match does not (both `""` and `()` render as nothing in a warn):

    sub ctx { wantarray ? "L" : defined(wantarray) ? "S" : "V" }
                                    perl    PCL
    printf("P:%s|%s\n", ctx(), "z")   L      V     <- printf
    warn "W:", ctx(), "\n"            L      V     <- warn, the same miss
    print "R:", ctx(), "\n"           L      L
    sprintf("S:%s\n", ctx())          L      L
    my @j = (ctx(), "z")              L      L
    join("|", ctx())                  L      L

So the context PCL imposes on those two argument lists is not merely "not
list" â it is VOID, which is the statement's own context leaking into the
operand.  Two members of the family, one rule.
subject: printf's ARGUMENT LIST is not evaluated in list context (print's is) -- a context-sensitive operand answers its scalar form and every later argument shifts
